about: Tests skipped on Linux: their reference library's Linux build differs from the Windows build whose bits the kernel gives (native/tools/linux_differences.py)

groups.opencv: Linux's OpenCV wheel (GCC) contracts multiply-adds into FMA in its AVX2 code, which the Windows wheel (MSVC) does not; the kernel gives the Windows wheel's bits
groups.opencv-daz: Linux's OpenCV wheel (GCC) filters this DAZ|FTZ case otherwise than its Windows wheel (MSVC); the kernel gives the Windows wheel's bits, which the B3 morphology manifest checks
groups.numpy-casts: NumPy's Linux wheel (GCC) converts NaN, infinite and out-of-range floats to integers otherwise than its Windows wheel (MSVC); the kernel gives the Windows wheel's bits
groups.numpy-clip: NumPy's Linux wheel (GCC) clips a signalling NaN under DAZ|FTZ otherwise than its Windows wheel (MSVC); the kernel gives the Windows wheel's bits, which the B3 conversion_small manifest checks
groups.numpy-nan: NumPy's Linux wheel (GCC) propagates NaN payloads and signs, and their FP warnings, otherwise than its Windows wheel (MSVC); the kernel gives the Windows wheel's bits
groups.numpy-fft: NumPy's Linux wheel evaluates pocketfft's twiddle angle in x87 extended precision, its Windows wheel in double; the kernel gives the Windows wheel's bits
groups.libm-and-opencv: the kernel's C-library math follows glibc's libm on Linux (cn_crt_math.h) and the reference's OpenCV step is the Linux wheel's: neither side has Windows bits here
groups.libm-and-numpy-fft: the kernel's twiddles call glibc's sin and cos on Linux (cn_crt_math.h) and NumPy's Linux wheel evaluates their angle in extended precision: neither side has Windows bits here
